tasks.goal: Implement the next self-host gap: freeze and pass a versioned ExecutionProfile and continuation policy from queue add through queue run to Supervisor. Add src/execution/profile.ts with fail-closed, bounded v1 types for ExecutionProfile (profileId, runtimeId claude|codex, modelId, providerId, optional endpointRef/accountBindingId, derived capabilities for mapped progress and provider-session resume), QueueContinuationPolicy (optional DeadlineExtensionPolicy and BudgetContinuationPolicy), JSON parsers, deterministic defaults for legacy worker/model, and helpers that convert a frozen continuation policy to Supervisor CLI argv. Never persist secrets: endpointRef/accountBindingId are opaque bounded references only. Newly added queue items must always own a frozen executionProfile; existing queue records without one remain readable and use legacy worker/model semantics. Store optional continuationPolicy on QueueItem and keep worker/model as an exact mirror of profile.runtimeId/profile.modelId when a profile exists; fail closed on mismatch. Extend queue add and add-plan CLI acceptance with --execution-profile <profile.json> and --continuation-policy <policy.json>; when a profile file is supplied, its runtime/model are authoritative and explicit conflicting --worker/--model must be rejected. Without files, derive and freeze a deterministic profile from explicit or default worker/model, with DeepSeek Claude/Codex defaults and opaque endpoint references. Validate budget continuation capability requirements (provider-session resume) and automatic deadline capability requirements (mapped progress) before dispatch. Make queue-runner pass frozen worker/model plus every deadline/budget Supervisor flag on both start and resume; policy values must come only from the queue item, not current env or mutable source JSON. Add a read-only pre-dispatch policy compatibility check that blocks Codex budget continuation rather than relying on the Supervisor error. Expose profileId, runtime/model/provider, capabilities and continuation summary in queue human/JSON control views and bounded queue events. Add tests in tests/queue-execution-profile.test.ts covering profile normalization/fail-closed parsing, secret-free provenance, default legacy queue readability, exact frozen profile/policy persistence across retry/resume, file input, conflict rejection, runner argv mapping, codex budget incompatibility, tampered queue fields, and status/event output. Add docs/evidence/QUEUE_EXECUTION_PROFILE.md and design/queue-execution-profile-v0.md with exact format, examples, tests and limits. Do not implement dynamic routing, admission counts, model selection heuristics, process-tree cleanup, manual continuation control files or a daemon.
nonGoals: Do not implement dynamic ExecutionProfile scoring or fallback routing.
Do not implement parallel queue dispatch or admission.
Do not persist API keys, tokens, raw endpoint URLs or account secrets.
Do not mutate an existing profile or continuation policy on retry/resume.
Do not implement process-tree identity or descendant cleanup.
Do not modify RunManifest acceptance authority or TaskContract.
Do not let queue policy values come from current environment at dispatch time.
deliverables: Every new queue item freezes a secret-free ExecutionProfile.
Optional deadline and budget continuation policies survive queue persistence and are passed on start and resume.
Incompatible runtime/profile combinations fail before dispatch.
forbidden: Do not store an API key, auth token or raw provider URL.
Do not silently ignore an unsupported --worker/--model/profile conflict.
Do not infer continuation policy from environment at dispatch time.
Do not touch files outside writePaths.
